---
title: "Architecture and Data Flow"
---

SCGSim keeps PDK facts, component intent, semantic geometry, solver preparation,
execution, result loading, and presentation distinguishable. A solver backend
may implement its own physics, but it must not redefine geometry identity, run
identity, or common provenance.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  PDK["PDK material, layer, fabrication, and 3D-integration semantics"] --> COMPILER["SCGSim semantic compiler"]
  COMPONENT["Component net, port, and topology semantics"] --> COMPILER
  COMPILER --> CORE["Immutable stdlib semantic facts"]
  CORE --> SGB
  SGB["SGB geometry, topology, and physical groups"]
  SGB --> PALACE["Palace backend preparation"]
  PDK --> AEDT["Declared AEDT spec and native family preparation"]
  COMPONENT --> AEDT
  PALACE --> HANDOFF["Run-and-handoff contracts"]
  AEDT --> HANDOFF
  HANDOFF --> PROFILE["Selected machine profile"]
  PROFILE --> ARTIFACTS["Immutable artifacts and receipts"]
  ARTIFACTS --> RESULTS["Solver-specific physical results"]
  RESULTS --> REPORT["Unified Plotly report envelope"]
```

The SGB path shown here is the current Palace geometry path. AEDT consumes its
existing declared portable GDS or Q2D inputs and family-specific specs; it does
not yet consume the semantic-core/SGB geometry flow. The converging AEDT
Surface-EPR work starts from the same normalized `GeometryBuildInput` source
facts, before SGB topology construction, and adds an AEDT-owned binding sidecar.
It does not feed Gmsh faces or tags into AEDT and does not reinterpret an AEDT
native observation as source geometry or contact intent.

## Contract boundaries

| Boundary | Authority |
|---|---|
| Material, layer, fabrication, Z/thickness, and 3D host facts | PDK |
| Component nets, ports, functional regions, and topology selectors | Component designer |
| Revision-bound material, interface, owner, side, and evidence facts | `scgsim.semantics` internal stdlib core |
| Geometry names, topology, Route A/B surfaces | SGB |
| Palace and AEDT implementation | `scgsim.palace` and `scgsim.aedt` |
| Solver-bound geometry inspection and preview evidence | `scgsim.visualization` |
| Run identity, handoff, profiles, receipts | One common SCGSim contract |
| Physical result meaning | Solver-specific, never flattened into a false common quantity |
| Report navigation, provenance, cost presentation | SCGSim report/resolver surfaces |
| Offline tetrahedral mesh diagnostics | `scgsim._mesh_quality`, exposed through `scgsim.palace` |
| Public component-simulation notebook source | OrPen SC PDK |

## Semantic facts boundary

`scgsim.semantics` is a solver-independent internal boundary. It accepts plain
values, has only standard-library dependencies, and returns recursively
immutable snapshots. A snapshot binds its source revision, geometry revision,
projection version, and canonical content hash. Detached serialization creates
new plain containers so a consumer cannot mutate the retained snapshot.

Every construction path—factory, direct dataclass construction, and
`dataclasses.replace()`—applies the same detachment, string-key, revision-kind,
and canonical-hash checks. Evidence patches and results carry the immutable
snapshot reference that classified them; a facade rejects missing or different
revision identity instead of silently rebinding evidence to its own snapshot.
Unsupported interface intent remains a classification-time error, not a
constructor-time validation rule.

The core records sourced patch identity, source and aggregate owners, declared
material and effective domains, explicit side meaning, sheet owner, and
outer/hole/seam provenance. Evidence states remain distinct as declared,
planned, or observed. Native observations enter only as opaque, detached facts;
Gmsh and solver bindings remain outside the core. Repeated observations of one
contribution do not create additional contributions, and missing evidence stays
unknown rather than becoming guessed contact.
Classification requires an established conductor and solution-domain role;
an observation by itself is evidence, not proof of physical contact.

The shared frontend boundary contains source polygons, holes, material and
effective-domain identities, Z/thickness, route representations, and
ownership. Source-linked junction declarations alongside that existing DTO
retain terminal nets, direction, dimensions, inductance, and capacitance;
those fields are not retroactively attributed to `GeometryBuildInput`. Palace
may lower the source facts through SGB into conformal topology. AEDT instead
creates its own native bodies, sheets, faces, and calculator selections and
records an explicit source-to-native binding. Neither backend may make its
native identity the other's input.

Material identity, geometry approximation, PEC approximation, and native
implementation are separate facts. The core classifies already-valid values;
the existing SGB and Palace adapters retain their source-specific validation,
error messages, and call order.

For Palace routes, PDK fabrication owns substrate materials and Z ranges;
component intent owns metal nets and polygon selections. SGB verifies
positive-area contact between the complete normalized face-metal and modeled
dielectric regions, including explicit holes, before Route-A substrate support
is recorded. A contact candidate cannot be inferred from bounding boxes.
Palace may request a generated background Region after those source facts are
declared. Its internal conductor-host reference allows construction and cuts,
but neither the Region envelope nor a coupon bounding box proves attachment
or creates a physical die-to-die gap. Existing authored vacuum regions keep
their own records and explicit unresolved host references remain errors.

The dev27 candidate partitions each Route-A sheet by exact local bottom/top
solution domains before SA/AA construction. It therefore preserves supported
MS/MA and synthetic partial-contact MA/MA patches without assigning substrate
support to an exposed remainder. Contact caps retain only the surviving side,
and a lumped-port footprint must belong to one compatible local patch. Route B
applies the same local evidence to finite top, bottom, and sidewall records.
Fully freestanding Route-A sheets remain unsupported.

Each patch keeps its semantic side contributions in one provenance ledger.
Physical surface kinds remain the Palace classification boundary: separate
MS/MA kinds lower separately, while two MA sides sharing one native surface
lower to one aggregate MA row with internal-boundary cracking enabled. The
ledger and the aggregate policy remain present in physical-group, index, and
report metadata; native output is not presented as side-resolved. Historical
records without a ledger remain readable and are not reconstructed.

## Current truth

The Human accepted the PDK/Component/SCGSim semantic-authority split and public
notebook ownership on 2026-08-16. SCGSim owns no public notebook source; OrPen
SC PDK owns the public component examples and calls the shared runtime directly.

The Palace Electrostatic/Eigenmode and version-locked AEDT runtime families are
implemented but remain `CONVERGING`, not V1 stable.

Palace mesh-quality inspection is an offline reader over the emitted MSH file.
It neither owns mesh construction nor starts a native backend. The reader binds
one immutable parsed snapshot to the file bytes and leaves mesh acceptance and
scientific convergence outside the report contract. See
[Tetrahedral Mesh Quality](mesh-quality.qmd).

## Palace preparation lifecycle

`ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` remain the public owners of their mutable
mesh, config, resolved-port, and handoff state. Their shared private workflow
only prepares values and persists caller-supplied JSON payloads; it is not a
base simulation object and does not receive callbacks into simulation state.

Both public `mesh()` methods invalidate derived state before checking
prerequisites. Geometry preparation then applies the existing vacuum, Route-A,
and indium-bump transformations in order and returns the prepared component,
stack, bump-fill record, and optional material mapping before airbox lowering.
The simulation conditionally stores that mapping at the existing point, so an
earlier transform failure or a non-mapping `materials` value retains the prior
mapping, while an airbox or mesh-construction failure retains the newly prepared
mapping. Eigenmode resolves authored ports before those transformations and
caches the resolved ports only after mesh construction succeeds.

Both public `write_config()` methods invalidate config and handoff state before
their existing prerequisite and mesh-existence checks. Solver-specific lowering
still occurs before persistence. A shared private writer replaces each
caller-ordered metadata file independently and replaces `config.json` last;
earlier files therefore remain after a later write failure, and `config_path` is
cached only after the final replacement succeeds. In-memory invalidation does
not remove an older config file from disk, and this per-file behavior is not a
whole-workflow transaction guarantee.

The shared stack loader, non-negative-number validator, and stack-material-kind
validator live in one private Palace input module. Electrostatic and eigenmode
call that module directly while retaining their public methods, invalidation
timing, shallow top-level stack copy, nested aliases, and problem-specific
orchestration. The older problem-module names are private aliases, not duplicate
implementations.

## AEDT execution lifecycle

`scgsim.aedt.run` is the sole command-line and AEDT Desktop transaction owner.
It validates one prepared handoff before changing its receipt, imports PyAEDT
only after that transition, opens and releases the owned Desktop, dispatches one
solver family, and gives the original family failure precedence over a later
release failure. Private HFSS, Q3D, and Q2D modules each own their native model
preparation, explicit solve, and export/readback stages. Families do not import
the transaction module, and their narrow shared native helpers do not import a
family or start a Desktop.

At family entry, one private bound request fixes the absolute run workspace and
detaches the parsed spec payload. Relative source paths are interpreted against
that bound workspace even if the process working directory later changes;
absolute source paths retain their authored lexical identity. Preparation reads
only this bound request after entry. Its carrier retains the mutable native app
handle together with detached preparation readback; solve and export consume the
carrier and cannot reinterpret a caller spec or workspace.

New preparation keeps the handoff and handoff-manifest schemas at V1 while both
declare that the mutable run receipt uses `scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3`. The initial
V3 receipt records a complete preparation-time SCGSim module manifest and
content digest. Before mutation, execution verifies the canonical manifest and
binds the initial-receipt and prepared-manifest hashes. A canonical historical
V1 `not_run` handoff with neither marker remains executable, but its resulting
V3 receipt records preparation provenance as `legacy_v1_not_recorded`; it does
not fabricate history.

Every completed V3 receipt records a separate complete execution-time module
manifest and digest while retaining the former runtime-source keys. Preparation
and execution identities are not required to match: their separation records
what prepared and what actually executed the handoff. Historical completed V1
receipts remain subject to their old resolution rules, except that a V1 receipt
combined with either later-version expectation marker is rejected as an
inconsistent cohort. Historical completed V2 receipts retain their existing
resolution rules; new V3-only native PEC checks do not reinterpret them. This
consistency contract is not source authenticity for an actor able
to rewrite the entire unsigned artifact set.

The frozen `runtime-source.v1` reader contract is distinct from the current
producer inventory used to emit it. One pure, versioned initial-receipt codec
owns the historical V1/V2 and current V3 JSON member order, indentation, and
final newline; handoff writing and initial-receipt reconstruction use that same
codec. A producer may emit the frozen schema only while its current inventory
matches the declared thirteen-module contract. Historical receipt hashes are
never compared with installed source, and prepared and actual identities remain
independent evidence.

Runtime-source provenance is computed inside the receipt-owned failure
transaction before PyAEDT import and Desktop construction. New HFSS V3 receipts
also keep source material identity distinct from verified native PEC
implementation: solids are native `pec` with Solve Inside disabled, while
sheets receive Perfect E and must have complete native face coverage.

The converging Eigenmode EPR lifecycle is an explicit additive path under that
same transaction owner. It does not reinterpret the historical one-shot
prepare--solve--export path or broaden the meaning of an ordinary completed
receipt. Before its one solve, the EPR path declares geometry bindings,
junctions, contributions, margins, calculator definitions, and native pass
cache items. After the solver stops it exports the recorded pass/mode history;
if the solve raises or returns failure, the transaction preserves that original
error, releases the owned Desktop, and performs no automatic save or partial
export recovery. The existing complete-convergence reader remains unchanged;
history exported after a successful solve records its own completed pass
identities and status.

Mode selection is postprocessing state, not a physical design variation. A
complete Eigenmode source vector selects exactly one native mode with the
dimensionless relative control `1`, with every other mode `0`, and binds phase
and the selected solution explicitly. `EigenPeakElectricField` names the
native normalization convention; this control is not a measured `1 V/m` field.
The vector order and persisted native source entries are evidence; inherited
GUI state and a synthetic `Mode` intrinsic are not. Pass-cache identity
separately binds setup, physical variation, adaptive pass, native mode, item
definition, dependencies, context, and solution. Item titles and row positions
are never identity.

Historical cache resolution and final saved-field analysis are independent
capabilities. The history reader returns only the pass/mode values that AEDT
actually recorded, preserving axes and missingness. Final analysis closes and
seals the solved project plus its complete result directory, reopens a distinct
working copy with solve guards installed, and evaluates the last saved fields
without modifying the original. Missing final fields do not fall back to an
earlier cache pass, and a new postsolve margin is a final-field calculation,
not invented pass history.

See [Folder tree and ownership](ownership.qmd) for repository placement and
[Headless Geometry Preview](geometry-preview.qmd) for the static and connected
Notebook inspection contract.
